item.title: EXCLUSIVE: Feds Say Fake Central Cee Account Drew In Crypto Scam Victim
item.dc:creator: Grouchy Greg Watkins (@GrouchyGreg)
item.description: A fake Central Cee account allegedly lured a crypto victim as federal prosecutors sought more than 50,000 USDT in a new case.
item.content:encoded:
Central Cee‘s name was used to lure a crypto scam victim, a Secret Service agent alleged in a new federal case.

The British rapper was not accused of running the scheme. The agent said an account posed as him to draw a person into a private chat group.

Prosecutors filed the case in Puerto Rico on October 19. They sought 50,221.254086 USDT, a crypto token known as Tether. They said the funds were tied to wire fraud and money laundering. The suit seeks to take the funds through civil forfeiture.

Secret Service Agent Nayit Limery Gonzalez laid out the claims in a nine-page filing. The filing called the person who lost the funds Victim A. The person found Snapchat accounts that claimed to be stars, the agent wrote. Those accounts linked to Signal groups with tips on crypto prices.

One account used the name “centralceenewss” and posed as Central Cee, the filing said. Victim A then spoke on Signal with a person the agent called Subject A.

“Victim A stated that Subject A advised them that he manages a group that studies the trends of the crypto market. Subject A stated he does not want any money up front, but that he would request 15% of Victim A’s monthly earnings as a commission for the tips on the crypto market. Victim A stated that Subject A had a British accent when talking to him.”

Subject A then sent links that were passed off as crypto news apps, the filing said. He urged Victim A to use them.

“These links that appeared to be for cryptocurrency news applications were sent to Victim A directly from Subject A. Victim A clicked on all these links and downloaded the apps from the links provided.”

Gonzalez said scammers can hide harmful code in what seem to be real apps. That was not a finding that these links held such code. Nor did the agent accuse the real app firms of taking part in the scheme.

Victim A said 32,451.558669 USDT left their Trust Wallet without consent on July 12, 2024. That was not the same as the full sum sought in the case. The agent traced funds through several wallets, where some were mixed with other money.

Gonzalez signed the filing on October 1. More than two years had passed since the reported loss.

The Federal Trade Commission has warned of fake crypto deals pitched by people who pose as stars on social media. It urges people not to click links in messages they did not expect.

People can claim rights to seized funds in this type of case. The Justice Department has said those claims must be resolved first. Only then can the funds be forfeited and returned to victims.

The docket listed a request for a warrant and seizure. Responses were due November 2.

item.title: Jaafar Jackson Credits Deleted “Michael” Scenes For Making Him A Better Actor
item.dc:creator: Nolan Strong
item.description: Jaafar Jackson discussed deleted "Michael" footage while awaiting sequel dates, with California approving production tax support.
item.content:encoded:
Jaafar Jackson said the scenes cut from “Michael” helped him grow as an actor. He was ready to play his uncle, Michael Jackson, once more.

In a new Variety interview, Jackson said the work that stayed off screen had “made me a better actor.”

He knew some takes would not make the film. The work still taught him skills he could use in other roles. He had heard other actors discuss cuts to their scenes, too.

He also said he had no solid start date for part two. His schedule was open, and he was ready to return.

AllHipHop reported in August that Lionsgate’s Adam Fogelson hoped to start filming late this year or early next year. The goal was to have the film out in late 2027 or the first half of 2028.

The studio has also won help to shoot the next film in California. California’s Film Commission announced new tax-credit awards October 7. Lionsgate’s “Michael 2,” a working title, made the list. The state’s project list puts the credit at about $30.8 million. It calls for 55 shoot days, with 65 cast hires and 300 crew hires.

The first film gave Lionsgate a big hit to build on. AllHipHop’s September box-office report put its worldwide run at about $1.029 billion. Most of that money came from fans outside the U.S. and Canada. The film passed “Bohemian Rhapsody” and “Oppenheimer” to set the biopic record.

Changes to the first film also reached beyond its lead actor. In April, Kat Graham said legal issues had removed her Diana Ross scenes.

Lionsgate’s notes trace Michael’s rise from the Jackson Five into his early solo years. Antoine Fuqua directed it, with Graham King as producer.

Jackson had also just finished his second film. He told Variety he had spent about 40 days in Australia on “Supermax” with Will Smith and a new cast and crew. This time, he did not have to sing or dance. “Michael” had filmed only in Los Angeles.

He did not give a plot for part two.

“My job is to come prepared and deliver the best performance I can,” Jackson said.

item.title: Leon Bridges Admits His New Sound May Have Driven Fans Away
item.dc:creator: Nolan Strong
item.description: Leon Bridges weighed the pull of his debut as his latest album with Jungle's producers took his sound toward the dance floor.
item.content:encoded:
Leon Bridges said his changing music may have pushed some fans away. He was grateful that fans could grow with him.

“I feel like some of my fans are married to my first album,” he told Esquire. The singer discussed that pull between old expectations and new work in a new interview. He said he still loved “River,” a track from that first album.

His debut, “Coming Home,” arrived in 2015. More than a decade later, his fifth album, “Happiness Anytime,” put dance music at the center.

Bridges told Apple Music that his last album, “Leon,” had been a slower, personal record. For this follow-up, he wanted songs that would get people moving. He said writing upbeat tracks on guitar could be hard for him. Working with Jungle gave him a way into that sound.

The 12-song Columbia Records release came out on September 25. Lydia Kitto, one of its two producers from Jungle, also sang on “All Day, All Night.”

The songs still dealt with his life, not just dancing. Apple Music’s notes linked “Talk It Over” to tough times in a relationship. He said the title track urged him, and his fans, to choose joy in good times and bad.

The shift reached beyond the beats. In Sony Music’s account of the sessions, Bridges focused on his singing, how the songs felt and what stories he told. Kitto shaped the tunes and how the notes fit together. Josh Lloyd-Watson shaped the tracks and arrangements. Bassist Pino Palladino also joined them in the studio.

The group made six songs in four days during an early Los Angeles session. They began work together in April 2025 after meeting at festivals. One early spark came from a few chords on keys and a drum beat. Bridges began singing what became “Your Love Is Electric.”

Their rule was to finish a full song each day, rather than leave it for the next session. Later sessions drew on Afrobeat, Brazilian music, soul and disco.

The goal also shaped the stage show. As AllHipHop previously reported, the live setup paired a vinyl DJ with horns and three backing singers. Kitto said Bridges wanted room to put down his guitar and dance out front again.

item.title: Did 50 Cent’s Rick Ross Beef Just Cross An Unwritten Rule Of Hip-Hop
item.dc:creator: Houston Williams
item.description: 50 Cent reportedly offers to bail out the man accused of pistol-whipping Rick Ross' son, bringing their longstanding Hip-Hop feud into troubling territory.
item.content:encoded:
50 Cent has apparently found another way to torment Rick Ross. 

But this time the controversy involves Ross’ son, an alleged pistol-whipping and felony charges. This is getting deep. I hope they are never in the same room.

50 Cent and Rozay have been going at each other for several presidential administrations. It makes Ja Rule seem like nothing now. Their rivalry was the gold standard for beef. But now, this one has taken over. This latest development takes beef to the next level.

Posting bail for the man that says this:”I don’t care who your daddy is, I’ll kill you right here.”? Wild!

According to reports from Florida, William Roberts III, the son of Rick Ross, was assaulted near Bethune-Cookman University in Daytona Beach on October 11. Police allege that 20-year-old Don Roberts III confronted the younger Roberts while he was speaking with a woman. Investigators believe the confrontation may have involved the suspect’s previous romantic relationship with her.

Things became frightening when the suspect allegedly produced a handgun and threatened Ross’ son.

Bold.

Authorities say the suspect then struck William in the head with the firearm after threatening his life. Fortunately, the reported injuries were relatively minor, and he did not require immediate medical attention.

The suspect was subsequently arrested and charged with aggravated assault with a deadly weapon and aggravated battery with a deadly weapon. Those are serious accusations, and he remains presumed innocent unless proven guilty.

But here comes 50 Cent.

The G-Unit mogul reportedly declared that he would bail out the accused attacker, while also accusing Rick Ross of involving law enforcement.

Now, hold on.

There is a substantial difference between making an outrageous statement on social media and actually putting money toward somebody’s release. At this point, the reported bail offer should not be confused with a confirmed payment.

And there’s another important distinction. The police account identifies Ross’ son as the alleged victim who spoke with investigators. That does not establish that Rick Ross personally called authorities.

Nevertheless, the implications are rather ugly.

Rap rivalries have always involved insults, humiliation and occasionally outrageous theatrics. But when somebody’s child becomes the subject of a criminal investigation, the entertainment value begins to evaporate.

I wonder whether 50 Cent is simply trying to get under Ross’ skin or whether he genuinely intends to support the accused man.

Either way, this is one feud that probably doesn’t need any additional ammunition.

By the way, Ross’s son is a real football prospect.

He’s like 6’2″, 270 pounds and built like a tank. He had a successful foundation as a three-star interior offensive lineman at high school powerhouse St. Thomas Aquinas in Florida. They captured four consecutive state championships. He went to Bethune-Cookman in early 2024. Suddenly, he was dismissed from the football team prior to this current season for alleged disciplinary reasons.

Anyway, has 50 Cent taken his rivalry with Rick Ross too far?

item.title: Busta Rhymes Aims To Break Grammy Drought On J Dilla’s Birthday
item.dc:creator: Nolan Strong
item.description: Busta Rhymes explained why a Grammy win with J Dilla would carry special weight as voters weigh their "Dillagence II" album.
item.content:encoded:
Busta Rhymes said he hoped to win his first Grammy with J Dilla. Next year’s awards fall on the late producer’s birthday.

In a Rolling Stone interview, he spoke about his push for “Dillagence II” to earn a Best Rap Album nod.

“It would mean everything because neither one of us has received a Grammy,” Busta said.

The show will take place February 7, 2027. Dilla was born February 7, 1974, and died February 10, 2006. The show will fall on what would have been his 53rd birthday.

Busta said Dilla’s mother, Ma Dukes, called him in November 2025. She asked how they could mark 20 years since her son’s death. He first set out to make a song, but that plan grew into the album.

That sense of duty also shaped the guest list, which Busta said he chose with care to protect Dilla’s work.

“Dillagence II” came out August 25 through Busta’s Conglomerate label. The set has 19 songs and runs just over an hour. It pairs Busta’s new work with beats from the late Detroit producer.

Common appears on “What We Got in Common,” while Talib Kweli joins “Love & War.” D’Angelo appears on “This Woman.” Ma Dukes opens and closes the album, putting Dilla’s family at both ends of the tribute.

Their bond reaches back to Busta’s early solo work. As AllHipHop reported in August, Dilla helped shape his sound on “Still Shining” and “Show Me What You Got.” Busta also paid tribute with the 2007 “Dillagence” mixtape, which DJ Mick Boogie hosted.

Dilla also produced for A Tribe Called Quest, De La Soul and The Roots. He was a founding member of Slum Village.

Busta has earned 12 Grammy nods. Yet he did not name a past loss he felt he should have won. He put his trust in faith.

“This is godly to me,” he said.

For now, the album is in the running for a nod. It has not yet earned one. The first round picks the nominees, while the final vote decides the winners. That last round runs from December 10 through January 7, 2027.

First-round voting closes October 22. The Recording Academy will name the nominees November 16.

item.title: 50 Cent Mocks Rick Ross’ Prison-Guard Past After Son Reports Gun Attack
item.dc:creator: Mike Winslow
item.description: 50 Cent used news of an alleged gun attack on Rick Ross' son to mock his rival's past work as a correctional officer.
item.content:encoded:
50 Cent used news of a reported gun attack on Rick Ross’ son to take a fresh shot at his old foe’s past as a prison guard.

The rapper shared a post about William Roberts III, who told police a man hit him in the head with a gun. He had also told police the man threatened to kill him. Rather than focus on the suspect, 50 took aim at Ross and the call for help.

“Damn got the man arrested,” he wrote, then asked, “why he didn’t just call his dad. He probably called the cops for him. LOL”

View this post on Instagram

The line revived 50’s long-running joke about Ross’ former job.

Ross worked as a prison guard long before he made his name in rap. He held the job for a year and a half. When a photo from that part of his life came to light, Ross claimed it was fake. The Smoking Gun then published state records in 2008 that proved he had worked as a correctional officer.

50 soon made the job a key part of their feud. In 2009, Ross took shots at him on “Mafia Music,” and 50 hit back with “Officer Ricky (Go Head, Try Me).” He also used a string of “Officer Ricky” cartoons to mock Ross, so the new post drew on a joke he had been making for years.

The case behind the new post stemmed from an alleged attack in Daytona Beach on October 11. William told police he had been talking to a woman on a sidewalk. A man then drove up and aimed a gun at him.

“I don’t care who your daddy is, I’ll kill you right here,” the man said, WFTV reported, citing the police report.

Police noted slight swelling on the right side of William’s head. He told them he did not need care for his injuries. He later picked a suspect from a photo lineup, though a check of city cameras did not turn up video of the attack.

WKMG reported that police arrested a suspect on charges of aggravated assault and aggravated battery with a deadly weapon.

item.title: AKA Had Fresh Injuries After Anele Tembe’s Death, Doctor Told Inquest
item.dc:creator: Mike Winslow
item.description: New medical testimony at the Cape Town inquest came as AKA's father challenged an earlier account of his son's injuries.
item.content:encoded:
AKA had fresh scratches and bruises after his fiancee, Anele Tembe, died. A Cape Town court heard the claim on Tuesday (October 20).

A doctor saw the rapper soon after her death, TimesLIVE reported. He found marks on AKA’s left forearm, right leg, right knee and neck. He said they appeared to come from sharp and blunt objects.

“The physical examination was done on the patient after exposing his full body. He had many fresh scratch marks,” the doctor said.

AKA worked with the doctor but seemed stressed and agitated, the court heard. The doctor said he could not get a clear account of how the rapper got the bruises.

Tembe, 22, died in a fall from the Pepperclub Hotel’s 10th floor on April 11, 2021. She had been staying there with AKA, whose real name was Kiernan Forbes.

The doctor spoke after the rapper’s father, Tony Forbes, raised doubts over claims about the marks. He asked why those claims had not been put to the test.

Forbes told Eyewitness News that Monday’s claims about scratches on AKA’s back did not match the medical report. He said the report did not list scratches there. He asked why no one had questioned that gap between the two accounts.

Those were the father’s claims, not court findings about how she died.

Forensic analyst Jeremy Philander told the court on Monday that he had traced the fall. He found that Tembe could have jumped or been pushed. His work did not settle which had happened. In his view, a slip and fall did not fit the physical evidence.

The state first chose not to file charges after it reviewed police forensic reports. It later sent the docket back for more work. The case then reached an inquest. That is where the court looks at how a person died and whether anyone can be held responsible.

This Cape Town case is not part of the Durban murder trial over AKA’s own death. Gunmen killed the rapper and his friend Tebello “Tibz” Motsoane in February 2023.

SABC News said the court was set to hear from at least seven witnesses this week.

item.title: Latto Celebrates Angel Reese Win At Arena That Moved Her Show
item.dc:creator: Mike Winslow
item.description: Latto joined Angel Reese after Atlanta's first WNBA Finals win, days before her rescheduled Chase Center date with Doja Cat.
item.content:encoded:
Latto joined Angel Reese at Chase Center after the Atlanta Dream’s first WNBA Finals win on October 19. The rapper had been due to play that same arena with Doja Cat that night.

The WNBA shared a clip of the pair posing near the court after Atlanta beat the Golden State Valkyries 79-65. Latto wore a red cap and black jacket as Reese put an arm around her for photos.

“THEY’RE SO ATL,” the league wrote. It posted the video at 10:50 P.M. Eastern on October 19, after the Dream tied the title series at one game each.

Reese scored 30 points and grabbed 16 rebounds in the win. Atlanta had lost all 10 of its prior Finals games. The Dream had been swept in three past trips, then lost Saturday’s opener to Golden State.

Latto’s own date at the arena had changed before the game. Chase Center’s event page named her as Doja Cat’s special guest for the “Tour Ma Vie World Tour.” It said Golden State’s run to the Finals moved their show from October 19 to October 25. Tickets stayed valid for the new date.

Latto and Reese had ties long before the Finals. Reese appeared in the 2023 video for “Put It On Da Floor Again,” Latto’s song with Cardi B. Reese was still at LSU then, and Cardi’s verse referred to the school.

Latto also went to Reese’s WNBA debut in May 2024, when the Chicago Sky faced the Dallas Wings at College Park Center in Arlington, Texas. In a courtside interview, Latto said she had come to watch Reese. She spoke up for women as more fans tuned in to the league.

“I’m here for the girl power period. Let’s go Angel Reese,” Latto said at the time.

This time, Reese played for Atlanta with a title at stake. Her team bounced back from a 68-64 loss in Game 1 and left the Bay Area with a split. Both clubs still sought their first league title.

The next two games were set for State Farm Arena in Atlanta. Game 3 was scheduled for October 21 at 8 P.M. Eastern. Latto and Doja Cat’s Chase Center show was listed for October 25.

item.title: Lil Jon Says Memoir Led To Discovery About His Biological Father
item.dc:creator: Mike Winslow
item.description: Lil Jon said his memoir led to a family discovery. He also returned to the finished book after his son Nathan's death.
item.content:encoded:
Lil Jon said he learned the man who raised him was not his biological father while writing his memoir, “I Only Shout So You Can Hear Me.” The book reaches readers on October 20.

In his ABC News interview, Lil Jon said that he had long kept his personal life private. His team urged him to tell his story, and he chose to share what he learned.

“I could have left that out,” he said.

In an interview with People, Lil Jon said he learned this after a cousin took a DNA test. His cousin shared the results, and the two did not match as expected. The cousin assured him they were still family.

Lil Jon said both his biological father and Willie, the man who raised him, had died, as had his mother, Carrie. That left him with questions he could not put to them.

“Neither one of my fathers are here anymore, nor my mother, so I can’t get answers,” he told People.

The memoir took another turn after the death of Lil Jon’s son, Nathan Smith. Lil Jon told ABC News the book was already done when he went back and wrote an epilogue about his loss. He hoped sharing what he went through would help someone facing the same grief.

Nathan, known in music as DJ Young Slade, was 27 when his body was found in a pond in Milton, Georgia, on February 6. He worked as an artist, producer and engineer and had followed his father’s path into music.

Lil Jon said fans of his meditation albums had told him the records helped them sleep and deal with grief. He hoped sharing his own loss could help people in the same way.

His 2024 album “Total Meditation” includes “Coping With Grief.” Lil Jon made that project with Kabir Sehgal.

The publisher lists the memoir at 304 pages, written with Paul Cantor. Its account of family loss sits alongside Lil Jon’s years in Atlanta’s music scene, the rise of crunk, burnout and his return to DJing.

Atria/Black Privilege Publishing releases the book in the United States on October 20.

item.title: Rick Ross’ Son Reports Pistol-Whipping & Death Threat
item.dc:creator: Nolan Strong
item.description: Rick Ross' son reported a pistol-whipping and death threat near his Daytona Beach college, according to a WFTV report.
item.content:encoded:
Rick Ross‘ son told police a man hit him in the head with a gun after a death threat that brought up his famous dad.

William Roberts III said the attack took place near his college in Daytona Beach on October 11. WFTV shared his account in an October 20 report based on police records.

Roberts said he was on a sidewalk with a woman when a driver pulled up and aimed a gun at him.

“I don’t care who your daddy is, I’ll kill you right here,” the man said, per the account WFTV cited.

Roberts said the man then struck him with the gun. Police noted slight swelling on the right side of his head, but he said he did not need medical care.

He later picked a suspect out of a photo lineup. Police checked city cameras but found no video of the attack.

Roberts plays football at Bethune-Cookman University. He is the son of Rick Ross and Tia Kemp, but his path to the school was built on years of work on the field.

The school announced his signing in 2024. He had played at St. Thomas Aquinas in Fort Lauderdale and helped his team win four state titles in four years.

In a 2024 profile, the Daytona Beach News-Journal asked Roberts what it was like to grow up with a star for a dad. He said that life in the spotlight had become normal to him, though he knew most kids did not share that life.

His ties to coach Raymond Woodie Jr. helped draw him to the school, even with offers from larger football programs. He also liked that he could stay in Florida.

“It just felt like home,” Roberts said at the time.

Once there, his goal was to help the team win. He told the paper he did not mind where coaches put him, as long as he could do his part. His choice came down to the bond he felt with the coach and the people in the program.

WFTV placed the alleged attack at McLeod Avenue and Weaver Street. Its report gave no motive or word of an arrest.
